name: us-state-tax
description: Dependency-free US state AND LOCAL individual income tax engine for tax years 2025 and 2026, covering 26 states plus New York City, Yonkers and all 24 Maryland local jurisdictions. Models what rate tables leave out: Maryland, where every resident owes a county income tax of 2.25%-3.30% on the same taxable income - a third to two fifths of the whole bill, reported by no table of state rates - where Frederick County's bracket selects one rate that applies to the WHOLE income so one dollar at $150,000 costs $360.03 while the same dollar in Anne Arundel costs three cents, where the local earned income credit is not stored but is ten times each county rate, where the new 2% capital gains surtax is a test rather than a floor so one dollar of AGI at $350,000 can cost $6,933.08, where the $3,200 exemption is a staircase that takes $9,600 from a family of six at one threshold, and where the itemized deduction limit is section 68 revived by a state; Massachusetts, which every rate table reports as a flat 5% and which taxes short-term capital gains at 8.5% and long-term gains on collectibles at 12% on half the gain; New Jersey, which has no federal starting line at all and whose retirement exclusion ends in a wall that costs a joint retiree $1,381 on one dollar of income; CalEITC, which is not a percentage of the federal credit but a triangle with no plateau; California's Young Child Tax Credit; New York City's 3.078%-3.876% resident tax and its 30%-to-10% sliding earned income credit; the Yonkers surcharge of 16.75% of the state tax; New York's supplemental tax, which claws back the benefit of the lower brackets; which federal figure each state starts from; which federal deductions it adds back; the state earned income credits and the four that are not what they look like - including Maryland's, which is published as a 50% credit and a 45% credit and is one credit whose effective match rises from 45% to 50%; and the credit phase-outs that make Utah's and Pennsylvania's flat taxes anything but flat. Every figure cited to the statute or state release it came from, and every carried-forward figure flagged as provisional.
